correctness.rationale: The site projectors are Hermitian, so Re⟨X,LX⟩=−γΣ||[P_j,X]||²/2 and every imaginary-axis eigenoperator is block diagonal with a diagonal E block. The Hamiltonian commutator of such a block operator is off diagonal, excluding nonzero imaginary eigenvalues. The same identity makes the semigroup Hilbert–Schmidt contractive, excluding Jordan blocks at zero and proving finite-dimensional convergence. Stationarity gives TY=CT and YTᵀ=TᵀC, hence [C,TTᵀ]=0. Its adjacent entries a_j b_(j+1)>0 connect every E index (including n=3), so C is scalar. After subtracting that scalar identity, W has both range and adjoint range in ker T. The cyclic recurrence gives nullity one exactly at n even and ∏a_j=∏b_j; here n is the number of sites on each sublattice, and the physical cycle then has length divisible by four. Conservation of Tr ρ and Tr Dρ determines the full stated limit for every initial density operator. For the localized example the recurrence, including the wrap-around at zero, gives amplitudes (−1)^j q^min(j,2m−j), and the squared norm gives the positive limiting site return in the stated order of limits. Changing any one bond nontrivially makes T nonsingular. An independent exact commutator calculation on the projector commutant found fixed-space dimensions 1,2,1,2 on four test cases, including a product-balanced odd cell count, a nonuniform balanced even case and an exactly detuned one; it confirmed the localized rational return with q=2/3 at n=6. This is a bounded check, not the convergence proof.
residual_risks: No bound uniform in size, detuning or γ is claimed. The size limit is taken after the time limit; the calculation is not a robustness statement at large finite time.

evidence: The all-position dephasing model uses projectors on every site; the fermionic model uses number dephasing on every site. Liu–Balu's generator uses graph-based edge/directed transition data rather than the selective site projections.
The standard fixed-operator commutant argument still requires determining the joint commutant and excluding peripheral oscillations in this model.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Tracing the actual jump operators distinguishes a stronger theorem on the same model from one on a different generator. In particular the unmonitored block remains unrestricted by the dissipator here, unlike under all-site dephasing.

evidence: The sparse-dephasing open path result is the closest generator-level analogue. Its arithmetic condition concerns wavelengths and integer monitor positions on a uniform path, not cyclic hopping products.

The distinct same-day hypercube and unequal-arm spider results concern coherent absorbers. They quantify dark-state capture and survival in different graphs, not trace-preserving mixing and dephasing on alternate cycle sites.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: None of these conditions specializes to necessary and sufficient cyclic balance with arbitrary positive weights; general existence of dark vectors alone also cannot imply that all other operators mix to the complementary scalar state.

evidence: The periodic zero-mode test is equivalent to (−1)^n∏(b_j/a_j)=1. Under positivity this is equality of products plus even cell count.

Yang–Molignini–Bergholtz give a geometric mode on one sublattice of an open odd SSH chain, protected from loss on the other. Wang–Zhang give extra zero rapidities from a zero-overlap mode for an open SSH chain with one lossy site.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Chiral zero modes and geometric amplitudes are not new in themselves. An open-chain recurrence has no cyclic closure condition, and the one-sublattice loss construction does not identify the full fixed algebra of this trace-preserving projector-dephased system.

originality.rationale: The dark-state recurrence and general dephasing framework are established tools. The supported distinct claim is the necessity of this product resonance for nontrivial stationary memory in the specified periodic, one-sublattice projector-dephased model, the resulting full asymptotic state, and its explicit localized-return/detuning consequence. The closest inspected frameworks and exact classifications differ in the coupling geometry, noise operators, or both.
residual_risks: A specialized periodic SSH selective-dephasing calculation could give equivalent coverage. No exhaustive literature or priority claim is made.

value.rationale: The entire graph remains connected with positive bonds and every site of one sublattice is dephased, yet the theorem distinguishes complete mixing from one persistent observable. Quantifying a positive local return after increasing the ring size, and its exact disappearance under one-bond detuning, goes beyond detecting a finite-dimensional kernel.
residual_risks: No finite-time noise robustness or transport claim follows from the ordered limits.
